overview: Funan, known from the reports of Chinese envoys in the third century, was the first of Southeast Asia's Indian-influenced states, in the Mekong delta. Its port at Oc Eo linked the trade of Rome, India and China.

items.text: Oc Eo's canals and warehouses handled goods between the Gulf of Thailand and the Mekong; coins of Antoninus Pius and Marcus Aurelius were found there.
Indian beads and seals, Chinese bronze mirrors and local tin amulets came out of the excavations of the 1940s.
Sanskrit inscriptions and images of Vishnu and Shiva show Indian religion at court, with Buddhism beside it.
The Chinese envoys Kang Tai and Zhu Ying, who visited about 245, described walled towns, taxes paid in gold and a written script.
A network of canals, one of them nearly 90 kilometers long, drained and linked the delta towns.
Funan set the pattern of the Indianized kingdom that Chenla, the Chams and the Khmer followed.
Oc Eo is among the earliest excavated urban sites in mainland Southeast Asia.

fall.text: In the sixth century the inland Khmer state the Chinese called Chenla absorbed Funan; by about 550 its kings ruled the delta.
